title: On‑prem canary eviction causing operator leader flapping and ephemeral KV cache rollback
creator: Jonah Kim
description: Multiple enterprise customers reported intermittent 503s and inference cache inconsistencies during a staged canary of operator v2.8 in Private/VPC clusters. Symptoms included repeated operator leader handoffs, tenant‑scoped sidecar restarts on a subset of nodes, and automatic rollback of ephemeral KV shards leading to transient stale model weights in serving pods. Customer support escalations arrived from two large tenants after automated canary rollback attempted to conserve capacity but left tenants in a degraded state.
steps_to_reproduce: 1) Apply operator v2.8 canary release to a subset of control-plane nodes in a Private/VPC cluster
2) Simultaneously trigger tenant rollout (small canary traffic burst) and induce node-level image pull retry by setting imagePullPolicy=Always for nodeagent sidecar
3) Observe leader election churn in operator pods (frequent lease renewals) and nodeagent crashloops on impacted nodes
4) Watch ephemeral KV shards migrate and rollback; some tenant replicas read stale KV cache until manual reconciliation
investigation_notes: - Early logs show nodeagent sidecar frequently restarting due to transient image pull throttling from private registry; restarts coincided with leader lease expiration windows
- Operator leader election defaults were tuned in v2.8 to shorter leaseDuration/renewDeadline values to reduce failover latency; combined with sidecar churn this produced repeated leader flips

- Ephemeral KV shard manager treats repeated leader changes as potential split-brain and performs conservative rollback to last checkpoint, which reintroduced stale model metadata for a small percentage of tenant pods
- Canary automation attempted automated rollback of release which accelerated pod evictions without waiting for graceful KV checkpoint completion
root_cause: A confluence of (a) nodeagent imagePullPolicy and private registry throttling causing sidecar restarts, (b) overly aggressive leader election tuning in operator v2.8, and (c) conservative ephemeral KV rollback logic that triggers during rapid leader handoffs. Canary automation lacked a guard to wait for KV checkpoint quiescence before initiating mass evictions.
mitigation_and_hotfix: - Emergency patch operator v2.8.1: revert leader election tuning to previous leaseDuration/renewDeadline defaults
- Patch nodeagent daemonset template to pin imagePullPolicy to IfNotPresent by default for private registries and add backoff jitter to pulls
- Update KV shard manager to delay conservative rollback when leader churn rate exceeds threshold and instead mark shards as 'degraded-read' until explicit reconciliation
- Short-term: manually reconcile affected tenant KV shards using scripted checkpoint replay and bumped shard TTLs to allow drift heal
- Customer communication: posted immediate incident bulletin and opened scheduled reconciliation windows for impacted tenants
rollout_plan: Canary v2.8.1 across 5% of clusters with monitoring hooks for leader-election rate, nodeagent restart_count, and KV rollback events. Hold for 6 hours; if no leader flaps and KV rollback rate <0.01% continue 25% then 100% over 24 hours. Provide automatic rollback trigger if any customer‑reported 503 spikes occur.
follow_up_actions: - Add an alert for leader_election_rate per-cluster with paging at >3 flips/10m
- Add registry pull latency SLI and make imagePullPolicy recommendations for onprem installers
- Improve canary automation to require KV checkpoint quiescence and to gate evictions on shard-stability signal
- Run a targeted test matrix for private registries (throttling/jitter scenarios) in staging
- Postmortem draft and customer remediation timeline to be published by 2026-03-12
notes_for_support: Support should coordinate tenant reconciliation windows with engineering. For affected tenants: run the included reconciliation script (linked in PR) and verify model response hashes match baseline. Offer a temporary dedicated rollback window if customers request immediate restore to v2.7.
